column1: # Key types Blindspot looks for. One line each, tab separated, most specific first: the first
# line whose start matches names the provider (in lines are tried before start lines, see at).
# After editing, run: bash tools/gen.sh
# id: lowercase letters, digits and -, nothing else (gird-fleet.sh and the shared counts drop any
# other id). start: fixed text, with one-character choices such as [.], that every match holds.
# at: start when a match begins with it (after any character in front of the key), or in for a key
# whose fixed part is in its middle: each of its starts is then written TEXT@N, the fixed text and
# where it is in the key (0 for the key's first character, after any character in front of it), and
# TEXT@N&TEXT@N is a start whose parts must all be there. A
# match is named by its in lines first, each tested at that place in the whole match, then by its
# start lines, so a key whose first characters look like another provider's start (an Entra secret
# that begins hf_ or with a digit) keeps its own name. in lines come last. max: the longest match kept, - for 300;
# a longer run of key characters is data. A pattern must not count more than 255 of anything
# ({0,300} is refused by the grep macOS ships) and uses no POSIX class or \s-style escape: it runs in
# grep, ripgrep, perl and .NET.
# A new id must also be added to PROVIDERS in gird.ai's Worker, or gird.ai drops it from the
# counts. Patterns are POSIX extended regexes that .NET reads the same way. Older OpenAI project
# keys are 48 characters after sk-proj-: 20, then T3BlbkFJ (OpenAI in base64), then 20; newer ones
# are 156 (OpenAI's community forum, GitGuardian's OpenAI detectors, gitleaks and TruffleHog).
# A key made on a person's own keys page, not in a project, starts sk-None- and has the same two
# shapes, and so does a service account's 48-character key, sk-svcacct-: OpenAI's community forum (thread 879912, July 2024) names sk-proj-, sk-None- and sk-svcacct-
# as the prefixes of new keys, 48 characters after the prefix until August 2024 and longer since, with
# _ and -. TruffleHog's OpenAI detector matched sk-None- keys from August 2024 to February 2026.
# An AWS key id counts after anything but a letter or a digit, as in an s3:// address after its /:
# glued to a word it is not a key, as with the other providers.
# A Bedrock short-term key is bedrock-api-key- and the base64 of a signed bedrock.amazonaws.com address,
# whose next 104 characters are the same in every key too (/?Action=CallWithBearerToken&X-Amz-Algorithm=
# AWS4-HMAC-SHA256&X-Amz-Credential=): 144 must follow the fixed start, so the start, or a key quoted
# only that far, is text about keys, such as this file, which an agent may have read into its session.
# A GitHub server-to-server token is ghs_ and 36 letters and digits, or, since GitHub's stateless
# tokens of April 2026, ghs_ and a JWT of about 520 characters with two dots (GitHub's changelog of
# 24 April 2026), hence its max of 1024. Neither may follow a letter, digit or _: words such as
# troughs_ and highs_ hold ghs_.
# Google's AIza and Replicate's r8_ keys must not follow a base64 letter, digit, + or /: agents keep
# pasted images as base64 in their sessions, and random base64 holds AIza and 35 key characters about
# twice in 100 MB.
# Microsoft's own scanning rules (github.com/microsoft/security-utilities, GeneratedRegexPatterns/
# HighConfidenceSecurityModels.json) give the shapes of its identifiable keys: an Entra app secret
# has 8Q~ or 7Q~ after its first three characters (SEC101/156); Azure DevOps and Azure AI keys are 84
# letters and digits with JQQJ99 at 53 and AZDO (SEC101/201) or one of ACOG's service letters A to o
# (SEC101/205 to 245) at 77, where c is Microsoft's dummy key (SEC101/233) and is left out; an
# identifiable Storage account key is 88 base64 characters with +ASt at 77 (SEC101/152). Azure
# DevOps documents the 84 characters and AZDO at 77 (learn.microsoft.com, use personal access
# tokens). Any Storage account key counts after AccountName=...;AccountKey=, as Microsoft writes a
# connection string (learn.microsoft.com, configure a connection string). A Cosmos DB for Table
# connection string is written the same way, its TableEndpoint after the key (learn.microsoft.com,
# Azure Cosmos DB for Table, connection strings), so its key is named Azure Storage too; a Cosmos DB
# key after AccountEndpoint= is not.
# A shared access signature (sig= in a URL) is not a key type here: the ones people meet most are
# short-lived links a service hands out for its own storage (GitHub's container registry and Actions
# artifacts), and from the text alone they can't be told from a signature for storage the person owns.
# The other platforms' fixed starts are the vendors' own, and so are the shapes their docs give:
# Databricks dapi and 32 hex (Microsoft Purview's Databricks token definition, SEC101/110); Slack's
# xoxb-, xoxp-, xapp- and xoxe.xapp- and its incoming webhook address (docs.slack.dev, tokens and
# incoming webhooks); Stripe's sk_live_, rk_live_ and whsec_ (docs.stripe.com, keys and webhook
# signatures); SendGrid's 69 characters (twilio.com SendGrid API keys); PyPI's pypi- and a base64
# macaroon whose location is pypi.org (docs.pypi.org, secrets), which can pass 300 characters;
# Sentry's sntryu_ and sntrys_ formats (docs.sentry.io, token formats); Supabase's sb_secret_
# (supabase.com, API keys). The vendors document the start but not the length of GitLab's glpat-,
# gldt-, glrt-, glft- and glsoat- (docs.gitlab.com, token prefixes; a personal access token is 20
# characters), Docker Hub's dckr_pat_ (docs.docker.com, access tokens), DigitalOcean's dop_v1_,
# doo_v1_ and dor_v1_ (its blog, April 2022), Vault's hvs. (developer.hashicorp.com, tokens: 24 or
# more characters after it), NVIDIA's nvapi- (docs.nvidia.com, NeMo Retriever API keys),
# LangSmith's lsv2_pt_ and lsv2_sk_ (docs.langchain.com, LangSmith administration), Shopify's
# shpat_ and shppa_ (shopify.dev, access tokens) and 1Password's ops_ (1password.dev, service
# account security): their bodies are the lengths public scanners (gitleaks, TruffleHog) use, so a
# wrong length misses a key and never names something else one. A Vault token needs 90 to 120
# characters, so the short tokens in Vault's own docs are not keys.
# A line #pass starts the next pass. Each pass is matched on its own, so a key of a later pass never
# hides a key an earlier pass finds, glued to it or one character after it. The first pass holds the
# twelve types of Blindspot 1.2.0, which so find just what they found before.
